questions.q: Where do objects and where do local primitive variables normally live in the JVM?
o: Objects on the heap; locals on the thread's stack
Objects on the stack; locals on the heap
Both objects and locals on the heap
Both objects and locals on the stack
questions.w: Each thread has its own stack of frames. The heap is shared. References on the stack point to objects on the heap.

questions.q: Thread A sets `ready = true` (a plain field) and thread B loops `while(!ready)`. Why might B never stop?
o: Without synchronisation B may keep reading a cached value
Booleans cannot be shared between two threads
The JVM kills any thread that spins in a loop
The write is always delayed by about a second
questions.w: The Java Memory Model gives no visibility guarantee for plain fields. Mark the field `volatile` or use a proper synchroniser.

questions.q: What does a happens-before relationship guarantee?
o: Actions in one thread are visible and ordered for another
The first action runs earlier by the wall clock
Both actions run on the same CPU core
The second action is guaranteed not to fail
questions.w: Examples: unlock happens-before a later lock of the same monitor; a volatile write happens-before a later read of it; `Thread.start()` happens-before the thread's actions.

questions.q: Which statement about `final` fields is correct for safe publication?
o: Other threads see correctly initialised final fields after construction
Final fields can still be changed by using `volatile`
Final fields are stored outside the heap
Final fields are checked only at compile time
questions.w: The JMM gives final fields special initialisation safety, provided `this` does not escape the constructor.

questions.q: What is Metaspace used for in modern JVMs?
o: Class metadata, held in native memory
The stack frames of every thread
Interned strings only, nothing else
Young-generation objects awaiting collection
questions.w: Metaspace replaced PermGen in Java 8. It grows in native memory and can leak through class loader leaks.

questions.q: A recursive method has no base case. Which error do you get?
o: `StackOverflowError`
`OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace`
`ClassCastException`
`ConcurrentModificationException`
questions.w: Each call adds a stack frame. Deep recursion exhausts the thread stack. Heap exhaustion gives `OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space`.

questions.q: What can the JVM and CPU do to code that has no synchronisation?
o: Reorder independent reads and writes if one thread sees no change
Never change the order of any statements
Run each statement at most once per second
Convert every field into a volatile field
questions.w: Reordering is legal within a thread's own view. Synchronisation (volatile, locks) establishes the ordering other threads can rely on.

questions.q: Why is double-checked locking for a lazy singleton only correct with a `volatile` field?
o: Another thread could see a reference to a partly built object
Volatile makes the lock itself run faster
Without it the class cannot be loaded
Volatile stops the object being garbage collected
questions.w: The reference can become visible before the constructor's writes. A volatile write prevents that reordering.
